# Local row stability for arbitrary corner bodies with fixed cutting chords

This note treats an unlimited number of vertices and curved boundaries in
one explicit geometric regime. It does not claim a neighborhood theorem
for all convex bodies. The restriction is that the three cutting chords
remain those of a nearby containing triangle; equivalently the double
sectors retain their actual triangular core regions.

## 1. Exact geometry and raw-data conservation

Fix three nonzero planar normals v_1+v_2+v_3=0 spanning the plane, source
zero, and a triangle T in which the three through-zero caps isolate the
three distinct vertices strictly. Let P_1,...,P_6 be its six intersections
with the cutting rays in circular order and put

    C_T=conv{P_1,...,P_6}.

On each triangle edge there are exactly two such intersections. Indeed
the normal belonging to the third vertex is strictly negative all along
that edge, so the two endpoint caps overlap on a nonempty middle segment.
The cyclic six-ray core contains these three middle edge segments. The
complement T\C_T consists, up to boundaries, of three disjoint corner
triangles. Each corner triangle is contained in the corresponding unique
sector, where exactly its vertex's cap margin is positive. This follows
also by evaluating the two other affine margins at its three vertices:
one is zero at one cut endpoint and the other is zero at the other, while
both are negative at the original vertex.

Let K be ANY convex body with

    C_T subset K subset T.                             (1)

There is no polygon or smoothness assumption. Each of the three sections
of K by a source cutting line is exactly the corresponding section of T:
K contains its two endpoints and is convex, while K is contained in T.
Write sigma_i for the corresponding coarea-normalized section lengths.
Let E_i be the area of T\K in the unique sector of vertex i. Then, exactly,

    k_K=k_T-E_1-E_2-E_3,
    Q_i(K)=Q_i(T)-E_i,
    sigma_i(K)=sigma_i(T).                             (2)

Boundary sets have planar measure zero, so no overlap is counted twice.
Conversely, a convex K subset T having the same three full chords contains
all six endpoints and hence contains C_T. Thus(1) exactly describes the
fixed-chord inner-body class.

## 2. The raw-data functional and its loss derivatives

For any positive raw data k,Q_i,sigma_i put

    M=sum_i Q_i/sigma_i,
    f_i=2sqrt(k Q_i)/(sigma_i M),
    Phi_1=f_1+(f_2+f_3)^2/4.

Let g_1=1 and g_2=g_3=(f_2+f_3)/2, and write

    e_i=g_i f_i,   C=sum_i e_i.

Differentiation with all raw quantities independent gives

    dPhi_1 = [C/(2k)] dk
       +sum_i [e_i/(2Q_i)-C/(M sigma_i)] dQ_i
       +sum_i [-e_i/sigma_i+C Q_i/(M sigma_i^2)] dsigma_i.

Along the exact loss parametrization(2), the partial derivative in E_i is

    partial_(E_i) Phi_1 = -alpha_i,
    alpha_i=C/(2k)+e_i/(2Q_i)-C/(M sigma_i).             (3)

Every quantity in(3) is continuous on the positive raw-data domain.

If T is tight at row1, alpha_i(T)>0 for ALL three indices. This follows
from the fully proved formulas in
`candidate 8e1d01c76d1a2560`, or from
the independent corner-truncation calculation. Explicitly, in the tight
triangle coordinates

    P1=(2v+w,-v-w), P2=(-x,x+s), P3=(-x,-s-w),
    x,s,v>0, w>=0,

put p=2v+w, b=x+s, c=x+s+w, e=s+w,
L=x+w+2v, B=x+2s+w, H=x+s+w+v, r=L/H, a=p/L, eta=4-r.
Then

    alpha_1=[eta(a-r/2)^2+r(r-2)^2/4]/(LB a^2),
    alpha_2=[b^2+e^2-(B/H)be]/(LB b^2),
    alpha_3=[c^2+s^2-(B/H)cs]/(LB c^2).

All are strictly positive because0<r<2 and B/H<2. Set

    a_T=min_i alpha_i(T)>0.

## 3. A uniform local theorem for arbitrary boundaries

**Theorem.** Let T be as above and suppose Phi_1(T)=2. There is a
neighborhood of its three vertices and a number epsilon>0 with this
property. For every triangle T' with vertices in that neighborhood and
for every convex body K satisfying

    C_(T') subset K subset T',       |T'\K|<epsilon,

one has

    Phi_1(K)<=Phi_1(T')-(a_T/2)|T'\K|
             <=2-(a_T/2)|T'\K|.                     (4)

In particular, every proper such inner body makes the selected row
strict. The theorem includes bodies with arbitrarily many vertices or
curved corner boundaries.

**Proof.** Strict source incidences and interior source membership are
open conditions on the triangle vertices. Within that open set, the
intersection points defining the six chords, their lengths, the triangle
area and all three cap areas are continuous functions of the vertices.
Their formulas are intersections of transverse affine lines and positive
polygon areas; no limiting section can vanish near T.

The three functions alpha_i in(3) are continuous at the positive raw-data
point belonging to T and each is at least a_T there. By the definition of
continuity, choose a ball in raw-data space contained in the positive
orthant on which every alpha_i>a_T/2. Choose a smaller concentric ball of
half its radius. Restrict the triangle vertices so that their data lie
in that smaller ball. Finally choose epsilon>0 so small that subtracting
losses E_i>=0 with sum E_i<=epsilon moves the raw data by less than the
remaining half radius. Such an epsilon exists explicitly because the
change vector in(2) has Euclidean norm at most sqrt(2)sum E_i.

All points on the path t mapsto(k_(T')-t sum E_i,
Q_1(T')-t E_1,...,Q_3(T')-t E_3,sigma(T')), 0<=t<=1, therefore lie in
the first ball. Integrating(3) on this segment yields

    Phi_1(K)-Phi_1(T')
      =-integral_0^1 sum_i E_i alpha_i(t) dt
      <=-(a_T/2)sum_i E_i.

The actual triangle theorem gives Phi_1(T')<=2. Equation(2) supplies the
actual K data, so this proves(4). No assumption that the intermediate
raw data describe convex bodies is needed for the integration: the
smooth functional is defined throughout the positive ball, and both
endpoints are the exact actual-body data. QED.

A proper closed convex subset of T' has strictly smaller area: any omitted
point can be strictly separated from that closed convex subset, and the
corresponding nonempty cap of T' has positive area. Thus the strict
conclusion is genuine whenever K differs from T'.

If several rows of T are tight, apply the same argument to each, taking
the minimum of finitely many positive neighborhood sizes and constants.
Rows already strict remain so by continuity of their raw-data functionals.
This gives all three row inequalities in the stated local fixed-chord
class. It is not an appeal to a minimizer or to unproved polygonal
approximation; the area losses are the exact data of the given body.

## 4. An all-dimensional version with an explicit geometric premise

Let a d-simplex T, d>=2, have a strict distinct-vertex cap circuit and be
tight at a selected joint row. The independently proved theorem
`candidate bb526889825517af` says that decreasing
k and exactly one Q_j by the same positive amount, with all sections
fixed, has strictly negative row derivative for every j.

Consequently the same continuity-and-segment proof gives a local theorem
for arbitrary convex inner bodies K of a nearby simplex T', PROVIDED
that their actual section measures are unchanged and all the removed
volume is partitioned among the d+1 unique-signature regions. The raw
data are exactly k=k_T'-sum E_j, Q_j=Q_j(T')-E_j. Simultaneous small losses
then strictly decrease every initially tight row. Curved corner cuts
confined away from all source hyperplanes provide actual examples of
this all-dimensional class.

These two geometric premises are retained explicitly. In higher
dimensions this note does not assert that any natural section core
forces them; in the plane Section1 proves them from the six endpoints.
Nor does the planar theorem control a body whose boundary gains or loses
area in a double sector, where a different sign pattern enters(2).
